prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Full Stack - Solution to upload Excel file and update database (Sql Script exists)
On upload of excel file, the columns in SQL database is updated.As of now the .NET code is hardcoded to columns present in Excel file. Task is to remove the hardcoded values and replace with UI where user can select the mapping of columns from excel to database.Frontend is AngularNote - Remote access to system will be providedBudget: $20Posted On: February 13, 2024 15:10 UTCCategory: Full Stack DevelopmentSkills:SQL, Angular, .NET CoreSkills: SQL, Angular, .NET CoreCountry: United Statesclick to apply
</job>

(none)

Style:
- Open with a generic line about being passionate and hard-working.
- Do not mention any specific past project or client.

- Write 300 to 380 words.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne — a passionate and hard-working full stack developer with 7 years of experience building clean, reliable web applications.

I’d be glad to help with your Excel upload and database update workflow. From your description, the current .NET implementation is hardcoded to fixed Excel columns, and you’d like that replaced with a UI that lets the user map Excel columns to database fields before the update runs. That’s a practical improvement, and I can approach it in a way that keeps the upload flow clear, flexible, and maintainable.

I’m comfortable working across both frontend and backend layers, and while my core background is in JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API development, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML, and CSS, I’m also used to collaborating with existing systems and adapting to the stack already in place. For this job, I’d focus on understanding the current import logic, identifying where the hardcoded field mappings live, and then replacing that behavior with a user-friendly mapping interface in Angular that fits naturally into the existing workflow.

A good solution would typically include:
- Uploading the Excel file
- Detecting and displaying available Excel columns
- Allowing the user to map those columns to database fields
- Validating required mappings before processing
- Passing the selected mapping into the update flow
- Keeping the existing SQL script and database update logic aligned with the new UI

Since remote access will be provided, I can work directly within your environment, review the existing .NET code, and make changes carefully without disrupting the current process. I also value clear communication, so I’ll keep you updated as I work through the implementation and testing.

If you’d like, I’m ready to get started and help turn the hardcoded import into a more flexible mapping-based solution.
